steps.tx: **Myeloma cast nephropathy**, also termed light chain cast nephropathy, is the most common cause of acute kidney injury in multiple myeloma. It occurs when excess monoclonal **free light chains** coprecipitate with **Tamm-Horsfall** mucoprotein in distal tubules, forming dense fractured casts surrounded by multinucleated giant cells.

steps.tx: **AL amyloidosis** is caused by monoclonal light chains, predominantly lambda in **75%** to **80%** of cases, misfolding into insoluble **7.5** to **10** nm non-branching fibrils in a **beta-pleated** sheet configuration. Biopsy demonstrates diagnostic **apple-green birefringence** under polarized light following **Congo red** staining. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

steps.tx: **Monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance**, designated as **MGRS**, defines a clonal B-cell or plasma cell proliferative disorder that fails to meet criteria for overt myeloma or lymphoma but produces a **nephrotoxic** monoclonal paraprotein that causes direct renal parenchymal injury. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

left.title: MGUS (Hematologic)
points: Clonal burden: Small plasma cell clone < 10%
Organ damage: Absent end-organ CRAB manifestations
Renal status: Completely normal renal function and urinalysis
Therapy: Expectant observation without clone eradication

right.title: MGRS (Nephrologic)
points: Clonal burden: Small plasma cell clone < 10%
Organ damage: Severe progressive monoclonal kidney damage
Renal status: Proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome, or decline
Therapy: Clone-directed chemotherapy to preserve kidneys

steps.tx: **Light chain deposition disease**, or **LCDD**, predominantly involves **kappa** light chains in **80%** of cases. Light microscopy displays **nodular glomerulosclerosis** mimicking diabetic nephropathy, while immunofluorescence demonstrates continuous non-fibrillar linear kappa staining along glomerular and tubular basement membranes. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

steps.tx: The phase 3 **ANDROMEDA trial** established that subcutaneous **daratumumab**, an anti-**CD38** monoclonal antibody, combined with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone, produces significantly higher rates of complete hematologic and renal organ response in newly diagnosed **AL amyloidosis**. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

steps.tx: **AA amyloidosis** arises secondary to chronic persistent inflammation including rheumatoid arthritis, bronchiectasis, and **familial Mediterranean fever**. Cleavage of **serum amyloid A** creates deposits that characteristically lose their Congo red affinity following potassium **permanganate** oxidation. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

left.title: AA Amyloidosis
points: Precursor protein: Serum amyloid A (SAA) acute-phase reactant
Underlying causes: Familial Mediterranean fever, bronchiectasis, RA
Permanganate reaction: Loses Congo red staining after oxidation
Target therapy: Treat underlying chronic inflammatory drive

right.title: AL Amyloidosis
points: Precursor protein: Monoclonal immunoglobulin free light chains
Underlying causes: Clonal plasma cell proliferative disorder
Permanganate reaction: Retains Congo red positivity after oxidation

steps.tx: The **serum free light chain** assay, or **sFLC**, evaluates monoclonal burden. The normal ratio ranges from **0.26** to **1.65**, shifting to **0.37** to **3.10** in renal clearance reduction. An involved light chain level exceeding **1500** mg/L, or **100** mg/dL, strongly predicts **cast nephropathy**. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.
steps.say: The serum free light chain assay, or sFLC, evaluates monoclonal burden, where the normal ratio ranges from zero point twenty-six to one point sixty-five, shifting to zero point thirty-seven to three point ten in renal clearance reduction. An involved light chain level exceeding 1500 mg/L, or 100 mg/dL, strongly predicts cast nephropathy. Careful clinical evaluation and regular monitoring ensure optimal therapeutic outcomes in these complex patients.

rows: Normal polyclonal kappa and lambda balance
Adjusted reference range due to reduced reticuloendothelial clearance
Immediate risk of tubular cast precipitation and AKI

steps.tx: **C3 glomerulopathy** in older adults frequently represents an unappreciated manifestation of **MGRS**. In these patients, a monoclonal paraprotein functions as an autoantibody that constitutively activates the **alternative complement pathway**, driving isolated glomerular C3 accumulation. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.
